name: bilt.me
evidence: Headline: Estonia’s bilt.me raises €615k with backing from Bolt and Lightyear founders to scale its AI-native mobile app builder

Summary: bilt.me, a Tallinn-based AI-native mobile app builder, has raised €614.9k ($700k) in a pre-Seed funding round. The round was led by Superhero Capital, a Seed-stage VC backing software-driven startups across Finland, Estonia, Latvia, and Lithuania. The round also saw backing from Bolt founder Markus Villig and Lightyear founder Martin Sokk. “We should be honest with […] The post Estonia’s bilt.me…

assessment.whatTheyDo: bilt.me is a Tallinn-based AI-native no-code tool that lets users describe an app in plain language and generates a native iOS/Android app, which it then helps preview and publish to the app stores.
matchedInterests: Agent frameworks, evaluation, and LLM tooling
concerns: Headquartered in Tallinn, Estonia, not the US — materially harder to join without visa/relocation or a permanent timezone gap.
Pre-seed round of ~$700K is below the person's preferred $2.0M–$150M range, indicating very early, unproven stage.
Founders are first-time founders in their early 20s, ~2 months old as a company (started as an August 2025 hackathon project) — technical depth is plausible but not yet demonstrated at scale.
AI app-builder / 'no-code app generator' is a crowded category (Bubble, FlutterFlow, Rork, Lovable-style tools) and risks being seen as thin differentiation beyond 'AI does the coding.'
assessment.rationale: Small team (6 engineers) building a real, shipping AI-agent product (native mobile app generation) gives genuine engineering leverage and touches on agent/dev-tooling themes the person cares about, but the very early pre-seed stage, unproven young founding team, sub-$2M round size, and non-US HQ all cut against strong fit. This lands as a weak-to-plausible match rather than a strong one.
assessment.summary: bilt.me is a Tallinn, Estonia startup founded in August 2025 by three founders in their early 20s (Uku Joost Annus, Kevin Akkermann, Karl Kiilaspää) that builds an AI agent turning natural-language descriptions into native iOS/Android apps. It just raised €614.9k (~$700K) pre-seed led by Superhero Capital, with angel backing from Bolt founder Markus Villig and Lightyear founder Martin Sokk. It's a real, small, shipping product but extremely early-stage and outside the US.
assessment.product: An AI agent that converts a plain-language app idea into a working native mobile app, with live preview on the user's phone and assistance publishing to the App Store/Google Play — positioned as a 'Shopify of mobile apps.'
assessment.team: Founded by Uku Joost Annus, Kevin Akkermann, and Karl Kiilaspää, described as still in their early 20s; the company reportedly has a team of six engineers and started as a hackathon project addressing Apple's app-testing restrictions, later going through the ruum hacker space in Tallinn.
assessment.funding: Raised €614.9k (~$700K) pre-seed, led by Superhero Capital (a Baltic/Nordic seed-stage VC), with participation from Bolt founder Markus Villig and Lightyear founder Martin Sokk as angels.
competitors: other AI/no-code app builders (e.g. Lovable-style web app generators, though bilt.me differentiates on native mobile output)
redFlags: Company is only ~1 month old at time of funding announcement (founded Aug 2025), with no revenue or user traction figures disclosed.
No careers page or open roles could be found, so hiring signal (e.g. senior/staff engineers) is unverified.
greenFlags: Team of only ~6 engineers — high potential leverage for an early employee.
Product is real and demoed publicly (they stream development on Twitch), not just a pitch deck.
Backed by credible operator-angels (Bolt and Lightyear founders) rather than only brand-name VC money.

name: Clastix
evidence: Headline: Clastix bags €2.9M to tackle the complexity of Kubernetes at scale

Summary: Italy-based Clastix, a company developingtechnology for managing Kubernetes operations at scale, has raised €2.9 millionin seed funding to expand its team and accelerate the development of itsplatform...

assessment.whatTheyDo: Clastix builds open-source and commercial Kubernetes infrastructure tooling (Capsule multi-tenancy, Kamaji hosted control planes, kMetal fleet-management platform) for running Kubernetes at scale with less hardware and operational overhead.
matchedInterests: Databases, distributed systems, and cloud infrastructure
concerns: Headquartered in Naples, Italy, and remote hiring is described as 'across Europe' rather than global/US — materially harder for a US-based engineer to join (visa/relocation/timezone).

All three currently listed open roles are go-to-market (Senior Pre-Sales Engineer, Sales Representative, Technical Marketing Engineer) — no engineering roles posted, which is a weaker signal per this person's preference for companies hiring senior/staff engineers.
Very small first-time seed round (€2.9M) with current hiring focus on sales/marketing suggests near-term priority is customer acquisition over product/engineering expansion.
assessment.rationale: Strong thematic fit (cloud-native infra/distributed systems) with credible technical substance — real open-source products (Capsule, Kamaji) with pre-funding adoption and technical co-founders — but the geography (Italy, Europe-only remote) and the complete absence of currently open engineering roles (only GTM roles posted) undercut the 'join as engineer, high leverage on product' fit this person is optimizing for.
assessment.summary: Clastix is a Naples, Italy-based infrastructure startup building Kubernetes multi-tenancy and fleet-management tooling, maintained by technical co-founders with enterprise Kubernetes operations backgrounds. It just raised its first external funding, a €2.9M seed led by CDP Venture Capital with Mistral and VERTIS SGR participating, to expand kMetal, its commercial platform. The product line has real open-source traction (Capsule, Kamaji) predating the raise, but current hiring is entirely sales/marketing rather than engineering, and the company is Europe-based/Europe-remote.
assessment.product: kMetal: commercial platform for fleet-scale Kubernetes operations (governance, cost, hardware efficiency), built on top of open-source projects Capsule (multi-tenancy operator) and Kamaji (hosted control planes); customers reportedly include AI labs, telecoms, cloud providers and public-sector teams in Europe and North America.
assessment.team: Co-founded by Adriano Pezzuto (CEO) and Dario Tranchitella (CTO), engineers with hands-on experience operating Kubernetes at scale in large enterprises; Gaetano-Kai Pastore serves as CRO. Team size not disclosed but this is the company's first external raise.
assessment.funding: €2.9M seed round announced 2026-09-24, first external funding in company history. Lead investor: CDP Venture Capital Sgr; co-investors: Mistral and VERTIS SGR (via the EU-backed Vertis Venture 6 Digital Sud fund).
redFlags: No engineering roles currently open — all listed positions are sales/marketing, at odds with the profile's preference for companies hiring senior/staff engineers.
Remote hiring scoped to Europe per company messaging, not US-inclusive.
greenFlags: Real, adopted open-source technical products (Capsule, Kamaji) that predate and underpin the funded commercial platform — not a thin wrapper.
Technical founders (CEO and CTO) with direct enterprise Kubernetes operations experience.
Investor Mistral is also cited as a production customer, a concrete technical validation signal rather than just brand-name backing.

name: Complaion

Summary: Complaion, an Italian company helping SMEsmanage certifications and regulatory compliance, has raised €13.5 million infunding to expand its team, develop its technology and support itsinternational gr...

assessment.whatTheyDo: Complaion is a Milan-based startup that combines AI-driven document automation with human auditors to help SMEs obtain and maintain ISO certifications and other regulatory compliance, with plans to expand into health & safety and GDPR compliance.
matchedInterests: Applied AI in a specific vertical (legal, health, finance, logistics)
concerns: Headquartered in Milan, Italy — materially harder for a US-based engineer to join (visa/relocation/timezone), per the geography rule.
No engineering-specific open roles found; careers page points to a generic LinkedIn listing rather than listing senior/staff engineering positions.
Founders (CEO, COO, CTO) came from McKinsey and Rocket Internet/Katoo backgrounds; no evidence found of deep prior technical/engineering pedigree for the CTO specifically.

Business model leans heavily on human auditors/expert review ('40 professionals', 1,000+ audits) alongside AI automation — unclear how much of the org is engineering versus operations/audit staff, which affects how much technical leverage an engineer would actually have.
assessment.rationale: Thematically this is a real applied-AI-in-a-vertical company (compliance/ISO certification) with genuine traction (900+ clients, 5x YoY growth, NPS 90+) and a credible €13.5M round within the preferred size band, which argues for a moderate score. But the non-US HQ is a meaningful penalty per the person's geography preference, the team mixes auditors with engineers so it's unclear how much of the ~40-person team is technical, and there's no visible senior/staff engineering hiring or technical depth signal for the CTO — so this lands as a plausible-but-thin match rather than a strong one.
assessment.summary: Complaion is a real, revenue-generating Italian startup (Milan) that uses AI plus human auditors to automate ISO certification and compliance work for SMEs, having just raised €13.5M led by Eurazeo and Italian Founders Fund. It's a genuine applied-AI-in-a-vertical product with strong traction, but the non-US location and unclear engineering-specific hiring make it a moderate rather than standout fit for someone seeking a high-leverage engineering role in the US.
assessment.product: An AI + human-expert platform that automates ISO certification documentation and audit prep for SMEs (up to 500 employees), aiming to expand into GDPR and health & safety compliance; claims 80% task automation and up to 5x faster certification.
assessment.team: Founded 2024 by CEO Edoardo Tarricone, COO Marco Cortinovis, and CTO Alessandro Vaccarino, who previously worked together running Italy for Katoo (a Rocket Internet company) and had earlier stints at McKinsey. Company reports over 40 professionals across compliance/audit and other functions.
assessment.funding: Raised €13.5M (~$13.5M per source headline) announced September 28, 2026, led by Eurazeo and Italian Founders Fund, with participation from Shapers, 2100 Ventures, Kfund, Sella Direct Ventures, Enzo Ventures, Vento, Ithaca, Eden Ventures, and Vesper. Nordic9 references an earlier pre-seed round.
redFlags: No specific engineering job listings surfaced despite a dedicated careers page — hiring emphasis appears to be on sales/audit/customer-facing roles based on available text (interview process centers on CEO and 'Lead Auditor').
Heavy reliance on human audit labor (1,000+ audits, 40 professionals) suggests a services-augmented-by-AI model rather than a pure software company, which may mean less pure engineering leverage.
greenFlags: Strong customer traction for an early-stage company: 900+ clients across 10+ countries, NPS 90+, 5x YoY growth.
Notable investor backing (Eurazeo, Italian Founders Fund) for a €13.5M round.
Addresses a real, unglamorous, high-friction vertical (ISO/regulatory compliance) rather than a hype-driven thin-wrapper niche.

name: Crux Analytics
evidence: Headline: Crux Analytics raises €1.9M to help banks win and retain small business customers

Summary: Crux Analytics, a fintech fixing the relationship between financial services companies and the small businesses they serve, has raised €1.9 million in seed funding to help institutions engage, acquire...

assessment.whatTheyDo: Crux Analytics sells a relationship-intelligence and agentic-workflow platform that helps community banks and credit unions find, research, reach out to and monitor small-business clients.
matchedInterests: Applied AI in a specific vertical (legal, health, finance, logistics)
concerns: The product looks like sales and business-development automation for bankers. How much proprietary data or technology sits behind it is unclear from public sources, so the thin-wrapper risk is real.
I found no live careers page and no confirmed open roles. The backend-engineer page surfaced in search but returns a 404, so I can't say they are hiring senior or staff engineers.
Community banks and credit unions have long sales cycles and slow procurement, which limits how fast the market can grow.

The team is tiny and family-run (three brothers, with one leading sales). Engineering depth is unverified: only one founder has a documented engineering background, at Wesper and Boston Scientific, and it is not fintech or ML.
The round is small, about $2.2M with about $3.2M total, so runway and compensation could be tight. Reports disagree on the size: tech.eu says €1.9M, while cfotech says $2.2M.
The lead investor is a bank-owned fund, which suggests distribution through banks but is not a signal of technical strength.
assessment.rationale: It is a real, shipped product with named bank and credit-union customers, in a vertical (finance) the person cares about, and a very small team where an engineer would have leverage. The score is held back by thin evidence of technical depth or a proprietary data moat, a niche and slow-moving customer base, and no verified senior engineering hiring.
assessment.summary: Crux Analytics is a New York fintech founded in 2023 by British brothers Jacob and Nathan Bennett. It builds software for community banks and credit unions to identify, research and engage small-business prospects, using agentic workflows. It raised a seed round of about €1.9M ($2.2M), led by Castle Creek Launchpad, and has at least two named customers. It is a plausible early-stage place to work, but the moat, market size and engineering depth are all unproven.
assessment.product: A relationship-intelligence platform for small-business banking. It scans the market and growth signals to identify prospects, researches them, runs personalized outreach and monitors client relationships. It integrates with existing banking systems and reportedly onboards in about a week. The first customers are community banks and credit unions, with plans to expand to alternative lenders, commercial insurers and real estate operators.
assessment.team: Jacob Bennett (CEO) is a former small-business owner and consultant to Fortune 500 companies and startups. Nathan Bennett (co-founder) has engineering and product-strategy experience from Wesper and Boston Scientific. Sam Bennett, a third brother, leads sales. Total team size was not found.
assessment.funding: Seed round of €1.9M (about $2.2M) announced 2026-09-24, for about $3.2M (€2.8M) total raised. It was led by Castle Creek Launchpad, a joint-venture fund with 34 community banks as limited partners. Chartway Ventures, One Washington Financial and Curql, three credit-union investment funds, also took part.
redFlags: The funding amount is reported inconsistently across outlets (€1.9M vs $2.2M).
No careers page or confirmed current engineering openings.
Value depends on data or workflow integrations that could be replicated by generic LLM tooling or by incumbent bank-software vendors.
The team and investor base lean toward sales and banking rather than technical depth.
greenFlags: A shipped product with named customers (Associated Credit Union of Texas, Bankwell).
A small team where an engineer would sit close to product decisions.
Investors are also distribution partners, giving access to a network of banks and credit unions.
A defined pain point in a large market: over 36M US small businesses.
The round is inside the preferred size range, and the company is based in New York, a preferred state.

name: Duqu
evidence: Headline: Amsterdam-based Duqu raises €1.5 million to unlock cash tied up in unpaid invoices

Summary: Duqu, an Amsterdam-based FinTech startup that gives businesses immediate access to money tied up in outstanding invoices, has raised €1.5 million in a pre-Seed round from Curiosity VC and No Such Ventures. The company has also developed its own AI underwriting engine, automating 95% of the credit assessment process. It also offers the technology as […] The post Amsterdam-based Duqu raises €1.5…
Headline: Duqu raises €1.5M to give businesses faster access to working capital

assessment.whatTheyDo: Amsterdam-based fintech that advances cash against outstanding B2B invoices (a short-term loan, not factoring) to Dutch/Western European SMEs, using an in-house AI underwriting engine that it also offers white-label to banks, lenders and lessors.
matchedInterests: Applied AI in a specific vertical (legal, health, finance, logistics)
concerns: Headquartered in the Netherlands and focused on Dutch/Western European SMEs (KvK-registered, PSD2 bank connections, Dutch-language site). Joining from the US would mean visa, relocation or a time-zone gap, and there is no evidence of US hiring or remote roles.

The core business is balance-sheet lending: 2.9% per month fees, credit risk and default risk. The tech is a means to a lending business, which is not the high-leverage software company the person describes.
The round is €1.5M (about $1.7M), below the person's $2.0M preferred minimum.
No careers page or open roles found, so there is no signal on senior/staff engineering hiring.

The technical depth of the founders is unverified. The one founder with a public background (Maas de Goede) has a ticketing/events and NEOM background, and I found no engineering or credit-risk pedigree for the other two.

The claim that the AI engine automates 95% of credit assessment comes from the company's own press release and has not been independently verified. It is unclear how much is proprietary ML versus rules and data aggregation.
assessment.rationale: The theme fit is partial: applied AI in finance and fintech are on the person's list, and there are real early traction numbers. But it is a small Dutch lender with no found engineering roles, a round under their minimum, and a material geography penalty for a US-based candidate. The evidence of a substantial technical company is thin.
assessment.summary: Duqu is an Amsterdam fintech founded in October 2025 by three school friends (Maas de Goede, Victor Brouwer, Diederik Nassenstein). It advances invoice cash to businesses within 24 hours and has built its own AI underwriting engine, which it plans to license white-label to lenders. It raised a €1.5M pre-seed from Curiosity VC and No Such Ventures, and reports about 1,500 users and €1.2M+ advanced. It is real and early, but a poor practical fit for a US-based engineer looking for a high-leverage technical role.
assessment.product: Short-term advances against issued B2B invoices for SMEs. Users upload an invoice and connect their bank via PSD2, and funds arrive within 24 hours. The fee is 2.9% for the first 30 days, then 2.9% per month pro rata, and the business keeps invoice ownership and its customer relationships. Separately, the AI underwriting engine is modular and pitched as a white-label product for banks, lenders and leasing companies.
assessment.team: Co-founders Maas de Goede (about 28; earlier built a clothing brand, events and ticketing businesses, and worked on NEOM in Saudi Arabia; studied at TU Delft), Victor Brouwer and Diederik Nassenstein. The press describes Brouwer and Nassenstein as de Goede's secondary-school friends. One source also names a Thijn van Helvoirt. Team size and technical backgrounds were not found.
assessment.funding: €1.5M pre-seed announced 2026-09-24 from Curiosity VC and No Such Ventures. No earlier rounds found.
redFlags: Netherlands-based with a Dutch/EU market focus, so hard to join from the US
Lending business carries credit-loss and funding-capacity risk
No careers page or engineering roles found
Founder technical depth unverified
Headline automation figure is self-reported
greenFlags: Shipped product with live customers (about 1,500 users, €1.2M+ advanced)
Proprietary underwriting engine built over about 18 months, with a possible B2B licensing line
Small founding team, so an engineer would likely be close to product decisions
Raised a modest pre-seed rather than a very large seed with no product

name: Granite
evidence: Headline: Granite raises €4M to bring its agentic cloud infrastructure to market

Summary: AI infrastructure company Granite has secured €4million in funding in a round led by Bifrost Studios, alongside private investors, to commercialise itstechnology and bring its software and hardware to...

assessment.whatTheyDo: Granite (graniteinfra.ai) builds a European "sovereign" cloud built for AI agents — modular, containerized datacenters (GraniteCloud) plus a network/orchestration layer (GraniteNet) offering compute, storage, and agent runtime (memory, permissions, tool access) as an alternative to hyperscalers.
matchedInterests: Databases, distributed systems, and cloud infrastructure
Agent frameworks, evaluation, and LLM tooling
concerns: Non-US: company is European (signals point to Portugal and/or Copenhagen, Denmark, never resolved to one HQ), which per the person's geography preference is a material penalty even if roles are remote-friendly within Europe.
A closed CPO job posting explicitly required candidates be based 'within 3 hours of CET' — suggesting hiring is Europe-timezone-only, not US-remote-friendly, unlike a typical globally remote startup.

CEO Peter Damm's background is COO/CFO and venture-fund co-founder, not an engineering/technical founder — the profile explicitly values founder technical depth, and no technical co-founder was clearly identified.

The round was led by Bifrost Studios, a venture studio that says 'we do not invest in companies, we build them' — Granite appears to be a studio-incubated company rather than an independently founded startup, which weakens the signal of external market validation.
Company is described as still in 'stealth mode' with 'first container shipping in 2026' — capital-intensive hardware infrastructure on only a $4M(~€4M) seed raises runway/scope concerns.
No current open roles could be found; the one senior role identified (CPO) was already closed as of July 2026.
assessment.rationale: Thematically this lands well — distributed systems/cloud infra and agent-runtime tooling are both top-weighted interests, and the hardware+software agentic-cloud angle is a real technical bet, not a thin wrapper. But it's pulled down by a non-technical CEO profile, a studio-built (rather than organically founded) structure, Europe-only/CET-constrained hiring signals, and thin public evidence of a shipped product at this stage.
assessment.summary: Granite is a European AI-infrastructure startup building 'agentic cloud' datacenters (compute, storage, agent orchestration) as a sovereign alternative to US hyperscalers, aimed at regulated enterprises and cities. It just raised a €4M seed led by venture studio Bifrost Studios, which appears to have built the company rather than simply funded an independent founding team.
assessment.product: GraniteCloud: containerized, liquid-cooled bare-metal datacenter units customers can own; GraniteNet: a network service to consume the same sovereign compute/storage/agent-runtime capacity without owning hardware. Includes 'Mycelium OS' (encrypted mesh networking/VPN) and a model-agnostic AI agent runtime with memory, permissions, and tool-access management.
assessment.team: CEO Peter Damm — described as a four-time founder with one exit, formerly COO/CFO in London for seven years, and co-founder of a still-active venture fund; no engineering background found. Xavier Leclerc (LinkedIn) is also associated with Granite Cloud but his role/background wasn't confirmed. No CTO or technical co-founder identified in available sources.
assessment.funding: €4M seed announced 2026-09-28, led by Bifrost Studios (a venture studio, not a traditional VC) alongside unnamed private investors, per Tech.eu and Startuprise coverage.
redFlags: Studio-built company (Bifrost Studios both incubated and led the funding round) rather than independently founded and externally validated.
Non-technical CEO background (COO/CFO, not engineering) for a deep infrastructure/hardware company.
Still in stealth with first hardware shipments not until 2026, on a relatively small $4M raise for a hardware-heavy business.
greenFlags: Addresses a real regulatory-driven vertical (EU sovereignty, GDPR/DORA/NIS2/EU AI Act compliance) rather than hype-only positioning.
Building genuinely technical infrastructure (custom datacenter hardware, orchestration OS, agent runtime) rather than a thin AI wrapper.
Round size ($4M / €4M) sits squarely in the person's preferred range, implying a small, early, high-leverage team if hiring.

name: Klang

Summary: Klang, a Helsingborg-based AI company that transcribes, summarises and analyses interviews, meetings and dialogues, has raised €1.32 million (SEK 15 million) in fresh capital at a valuation of €13.2 million (SEK 150 million). assessment.whatTheyDo: Klang builds proprietary speech and language AI (including an open-source Swedish speech-to-text model, Pianissimo) that transcribes, summarizes, and makes searchable the conversations of legal, public-sector, and research organizations.
matchedInterests: Applied AI in a specific vertical (legal, health, finance, logistics)
concerns: Headquartered in Helsingborg, Sweden with roles explicitly hybrid Helsingborg/Stockholm — no evidence of US-based or fully remote hiring, so this is materially harder for a US-based candidate to join (visa/relocation/timezone).

assessment.summary: Klang (klang.ai) is a Helsingborg, Sweden-based applied-AI company building proprietary speech/language models for transcribing and analyzing conversations (meetings, interviews, legal/public-sector dialogues), recently raising €1.32M at a €13.2M valuation on top of existing SEK 20M ARR. assessment.funding: Raised SEK 15M (~€1.32M / ~$1.4M) in September 2026 at a SEK 150M (~€13.2M) valuation, led by angel investors Johan Lenander, Emil Sjödin (founder of Refined), and Daniel Gadd (co-founder of Position Green), with participation from existing shareholders. redFlags: No remote-to-US hiring signal; all listed roles are hybrid in Helsingborg or Stockholm, Sweden.
greenFlags: Real, disclosed revenue (~SEK 20M ARR) rather than a pre-product raise.
Shipped and open-sourced a proprietary, benchmarked speech model (Pianissimo) rather than wrapping a third-party API.
Technical founding team with prior startup/engineering track record (CTO of an 8-engineer team through a 2017 acquisition).
Hiring for senior/staff engineering and research roles, with careers page explicitly emphasizing staying 'close to the technology, the users and the decisions.'

name: Kontext
evidence: Headline: Kontext raises $4M for runtime security platform for AI agents

Summary: AI security company Kontext has raised $4million in funding to expand its runtime security platform for AI agents. Thefinancing was led by 42CAP, with backing from a16z CSX and HTGF.Founded by Jens Er...

assessment.whatTheyDo: Kontext builds a runtime security and authorization layer for AI agents: it hooks tool calls from coding agents such as Claude Code, Codex and Cowork, checks them against policy before they run, and brokers short-lived scoped credentials.
matchedInterests: Agent frameworks, evaluation, and LLM tooling
concerns: Headquartered in Munich, Germany, so it is materially harder for a US-based person to join (visa, relocation, time-zone gap). Score lowered for this. The company is not clearly remote-friendly for US hires, and I found no evidence of a US presence.
Very early: about 4 people per one press report (TFN), pre-revenue, with only unnamed design partners, mostly in financial services.
No careers page or open roles found. The press release says the money will 'expand the engineering team', but there is no evidence of senior or staff engineering hiring.
Crowded and fast-moving category (agent identity and authorization). Large vendors and other startups could absorb it, and the moat may be little more than being early.
Small team and thin sourcing: headcount and founder background details come mostly from one outlet.
assessment.rationale: The product is real: open-source repos, docs, published pricing tiers and a technical credential-broker design using RFC 8693 token exchange. It sits in agent tooling and security, which are strong themes for this person. The Germany HQ, a 4-person pre-revenue team and no visible hiring data hold the score to the plausible-match range.
assessment.summary: Kontext is a Munich-based seed-stage startup, founded in early 2025, that builds runtime authorization and security for AI agents. It has raised $4M led by 42CAP with a16z CSX and HTGF. The engineering looks genuine and is partly open source, but the team is tiny, the company is pre-revenue, and it is based outside the US. That makes it a long shot for a US-based engineer unless it opens US or remote roles.
assessment.product: A local daemon and platform that sits between AI agents (Claude Code, Codex, Cowork) and the tools they use. It inspects each tool call against policy before execution (observe mode first, then enforce), brokers short-lived scoped OAuth credentials (GitHub, Slack, Linear, any OAuth or API-key service) and keeps audit traces. Pricing is listed as Starter (free), Pro ($149/mo) and Scale ($499/mo). Aimed at teams and enterprises deploying coding agents, especially in financial services.
assessment.team: Jens Ernstberger (co-founder and CEO) has a PhD in systems security and applied cryptography and did a research internship at a16z Crypto. Michel Osswald (co-founder) studied electrical engineering and moved into cybersecurity. TFN reports a team of 4.
assessment.funding: $4M seed announced 2026-09-24, led by 42CAP with a16z CSX and HTGF (High-Tech Gründerfonds). No earlier rounds found.
techStack: Claude Code, Codex and Cowork hooks
redFlags: Non-US headquarters (Munich)
Pre-revenue with only unnamed design partners
No careers page or open roles found
About 4 employees, so the company is early and fragile
Crowded agent-security category
greenFlags: Technical founders with cryptography and systems-security depth
Open-source code (kontext-cli and kontext repos) and public docs show a shipped product
Seed size ($4M) is proportionate and not an inflated raise
At 4 people, an engineer would have very high leverage and be close to product decisions
Timely problem: authorizing what AI agents do at runtime

name: Magic AI
evidence: Headline: Magic AI raises £8m to take its AI-powered fitness mirror to the US

assessment.whatTheyDo: London-based maker of the MAGIC AI Mirror, a wall-mounted smart fitness mirror that uses proprietary ReflectAI computer vision to count reps, correct form and project hologram trainers, sold to consumers by subscription.
concerns: Headquartered in London, UK and hiring appears London-centric (the one role I found, Product Owner, is hybrid London HQ), so it is materially harder for a US-based person to join. US expansion is led by a go-to-market hire, not engineering.
Consumer hardware business: capital-intensive, with fitness-mirror category history that is poor (Mirror, Tonal and Peloton struggled), so the market may not get large.
Positioning is partly celebrity/brand-driven (Jesse Lingard, Alastair Cook as trainers and investors), which fits the person's skepticism of hype-driven positioning.
Funding is described inconsistently across outlets: £8M is roughly $11M, not $8M as in the prompt. Prior figures ($9M seed, $5M, $2.5M) also conflict between sources.
No evidence found of senior/staff engineering openings or of the engineering team's size or depth. The careers listing (Workable) could not be loaded, and no CTO was identified by name.
assessment.rationale: There is a real shipped product with proprietary computer vision (ReflectAI, trained on 500k+ coached workouts), and it has a King's Award and reported 342% annual growth, which counts in its favour. However, this is a consumer hardware/fitness company headquartered in the UK, the US push is a sales and market-entry effort, and I found no evidence of engineering roles or leverage for a US-based engineer. The fit is weak-to-moderate, and it is penalised for the non-US HQ.
assessment.summary: MAGIC AI, founded in 2021 by Varun Bhanot (CEO) and Sunil Jindal (AI), sells an AI fitness mirror with proprietary computer vision, and has raised about $20M in total including a £8M (~$11M) Series B co-led by Beringea and IW Capital in September 2026. The product is real and shipping, with 18,000+ US members across all 50 states, but it is a UK consumer hardware business. It is a modest match for this person because of the geography and the lack of visible engineering openings.
assessment.product: Wall-mounted smart mirror plus subscription content. ReflectAI computer vision tracks about 845 exercises, counts reps, gives live form correction and projects hologram trainers. Sold direct to consumers in the UK and US, and stocked in Selfridges.
assessment.team: Co-founders Varun Bhanot (CEO, tech entrepreneur; award-winning) and Sunil Jindal (AI expert), per press. A former Peloton managing director was hired to lead US market entry. Engineering team size and backgrounds not found.
assessment.funding: About $20M total. Roughly $9M seed (Oct 2023) and a ~$5M round in 2024, plus angel money from Alastair Cook and Jesse Lingard. September 2026 Series B of £8M (~$11M) co-led by Beringea and IW Capital, with new backer Active Partners and returning investors PXN Group, Accelerate Ventures and Ventures Together. Sources disagree on some earlier figures.
openRoles: Product Owner (hybrid, London HQ; listed at $90,000-$110,000 per SportsTechJobs)
redFlags: UK headquarters; US role locations unconfirmed
Consumer hardware fitness category with a record of struggling companies
Celebrity-driven marketing
No evidence of senior/staff engineering hiring
Conflicting funding figures across press
greenFlags: Shipped product with real users (18,000+ US members)
Proprietary computer vision model trained on a sizeable in-house dataset
Reported 342% annual growth
Founders include a dedicated AI co-founder
King's Award and Fast Company 2026 Most Innovative Companies recognition
Round size is within the preferred range

name: Morphotonics
evidence: Headline: Morphotonics raises €40M to expand its display tech into data centers
Summary: Deep tech company Morphotonics raises €40M from investors including 3M Ventures, Innovation Industries, BOM, and Invest-NL.

assessment.whatTheyDo: Builds large-area nanoimprint lithography (NIL) equipment, processes and proprietary materials used to manufacture AR/smart-glasses waveguides and other nano-optics, and is now expanding into co-packaged optics for data centers.
concerns: Headquartered in Veldhoven, Netherlands, with a lab and factory-floor workforce. This is materially harder for a US-based person to join (visa, relocation, time zone), and there is no sign of US hiring.

It is a semiconductor and optics equipment company. Its core work is optical, mechanical and process engineering, so it has little overlap with the person's software, AI, infrastructure or consumer interests.

The careers page currently shows 'No Vacancies Found'. Job boards list roles such as Principal C# Engineer, procurement, supply chain and program management, but I found no senior or staff software roles close to product decisions.
At about 60 people and a €40M round, it is small but capital-intensive. Value comes from hardware manufacturing and a few dozen equipment placements, not from software leverage.
Its data center pivot is an early-stage expansion, described in press only as development of co-packaged optics.
assessment.rationale: This is a real, technically deep operating company with shipped machines, but it is a European photonics manufacturing-equipment business. Only the low-weight hardware theme matches, and the non-US location plus a lack of software roles make it a poor place for this person to work. The score is low but not zero because the technology and product are real.
assessment.summary: Morphotonics is a Dutch company, founded around 2014, that makes large-area nanoimprint lithography equipment for producing waveguides in smart glasses. Its customers reportedly include the supply chains for Meta Ray-Ban, Magic Leap and Even Reality. It raised €40M in September 2026 to scale production and enter data-center co-packaged optics. It is a credible deep-tech company, but it is far from this person's software/AI focus and is based in the Netherlands.
assessment.product: NIL manufacturing systems, processes and proprietary materials for making AR/smart-glasses waveguides and nano-optics for consumer electronics makers. A next-generation machine is planned for early 2027 with a capacity of more than 6 million waveguides a year. Co-packaged optics for data centers using photonic integrated circuits is in development. About 10–15 systems are deployed, with a target of 50 in two to three years.
assessment.team: CEO Hugo da Silva joined in September 2024. The team has about 60 employees, up from roughly 30 in 2024, with a plan to reach 70–75. I did not verify the founders' backgrounds.
assessment.funding: €40M (about $40M) announced September 2026, as the close of an extended round that began with a €10M Series B first closing in 2024. Named investors are 3M Ventures, Innovation Industries, BOM, Invest-NL, the European Innovation Council Fund, Ernij Next (a Dutch family office) and the European Investment Bank.
techStack: C# (per a job board listing for a Principal C# Engineer)
redFlags: Non-US headquarters with no evidence of US or remote hiring
No open roles on the official careers page
Hardware and equipment business with limited software leverage
The data center pivot is unproven
greenFlags: About 12 years of real technology development with shipped systems in the field
Customers in the smart-glasses supply chain, reportedly including Meta Ray-Ban, Magic Leap and Even Reality
The team roughly doubled in two years to about 60 people
Strategic investors including 3M Ventures and the EIB
Its data-center optics push targets the AI interconnect bottleneck, a large market

name: Quartermaster
evidence: Headline: Ocean surveillance startup Quartermaster raises another $140M
Summary: The tech enables real-time awareness for what Quartermaster calls the “largest blind spot on Earth.”

assessment.whatTheyDo: Quartermaster builds SmartMast, a hardware sensor package (cameras + radios) mounted on ship masts that converts ordinary vessels into a distributed real-time maritime awareness network, using AI to analyze the captured video/data for collision avoidance, security, and rescue use cases.
matchedInterests: Applied AI in a specific vertical (legal, health, finance, logistics)
concerns: Headquartered in Arlington, VA — not one of the preferred states (CA/NY/WA/MA), though still domestic so only mildly penalized.

Careers page currently states 'we're not hiring right now' aside from an opportunity-hire form; only one concrete open role found (Senior Mechanical Engineer) via a job aggregator, not a strong senior/staff software engineering hiring signal.

Leadership and customer base skew defense/government-adjacent (COO ex-Scale AI + 13 years US Navy reservist, CGO ex-Anduril/DARPA, customers include navies and coast guards) — the person said they're not interested in defense/weapons systems; this isn't a weapons platform, but it's clearly intertwined with military/government customers.

Raised ~$183M combined across Series A ($43M, May 2026) and Series B ($140M, Sept 2026) within about four months — a very large amount of capital for a company whose total headcount isn't disclosed, worth probing for team size and burn.
assessment.rationale: This is a real, shipping hardware+AI product (650+ vessels, 800+ SmartMast units across 25 countries) with a technically credible founder and reputable institutional investors (Insight Partners, First Round Capital, Quiet Capital), which argues for a legitimate vertical-AI infrastructure company rather than hype. It loses points because it's not in a preferred metro, has no visible active senior engineering hiring push, and its defense/government customer and leadership overlap sits close to an explicit anti-theme even though the product itself is civilian maritime safety rather than weapons.
assessment.summary: Quartermaster (Arlington, VA) is a maritime domain awareness startup that outfits ships with camera/radio hardware (SmartMast) to build a real-time sensing network for the ocean, serving coast guards, navies, insurers, and shipping operators. It just raised a $140M Series B (led by Insight Partners) on top of a $43M Series A four months earlier, with real deployed hardware and named, credible investors.
assessment.product: SmartMast: weather-hardened onboard sensor hardware (cameras, radios) plus a cloud/AI backend that turns vessels into nodes of a real-time maritime sensing network, used for collision avoidance, shipping-lane analytics, illegal fishing/security detection, and search-and-rescue support.
assessment.team: Founder/CEO Neil Sobin has a background in distributed networks, AI, and edge data/mapping technology. COO Matt Beck spent 13 years active duty in the US Navy (still a reservist) and previously worked at Scale AI and on Air Force software programs. CGO Steve Ribaudo has 20+ years in gov/enterprise tech with prior roles at Anduril, DARPA, and federal service.
assessment.funding: Series A: $43M (May 2026), co-led by First Round Capital and Quiet Capital. Series B: $140M (Sept 2026), led by Insight Partners with participation from Overmatch Ventures and First Round Capital, plus a $40M debt facility from Stifel.
techStack: Computer vision / AI video analysis for maritime detection
Real-time distributed sensor network / data pipeline
redFlags: No confirmed open senior/staff software engineering roles at time of research; only a Senior Mechanical Engineer listing surfaced via a job aggregator.

Heavy defense/government customer and leadership ties (Navy, Anduril, DARPA, Scale AI) run close to the person's stated disinterest in defense/weapons work, even though the product is civilian surveillance rather than armaments.
greenFlags: Real, shipped hardware+software product with 650+ vessels and 800+ units deployed across 25 countries — not vaporware or a thin wrapper.
Backed by credible, named investors (Insight Partners, First Round Capital, Quiet Capital) rather than only hype-driven funds.

Founder has genuine technical depth in distributed systems/AI, and the vertical (ocean/maritime data) has essentially no incumbent digital infrastructure, suggesting a real, defensible market rather than a copycat AI wrapper.

name: Reactive Technologies
evidence: Headline: London’s Reactive Technologies secures €19 million EIB financing to strengthen Europe’s power grids

Summary: Reactive Technologies, a London-based power-grid technology company, has secured €19 million in financing from the European Investment Bank (EIB) to promote its platform, which aims to reduce the risk of electricity outages, lower grid operating costs, and increase the supply of clean energy in Europe. The company states that its platform, GridVerix, provides real-time measurements […] The post…

assessment.whatTheyDo: Reactive Technologies builds Grid-Sonar/GridVerix, hardware-and-software systems that measure real-time grid inertia and stability for electric utilities and grid operators.
concerns: Headquartered in London, UK, not the US — materially harder to join (visa/relocation/time-zone) per the person's stated geography preference.

Company was founded in 2010 (16 years old) with ~50-79 employees and $94.6M+ raised — this is a mature, mid-size deep-tech firm, not a small early-stage team where an engineer would have outsized leverage.
The €19M raise reported is EIB debt financing, not a typical equity venture round, so it's a weaker signal of investor conviction than a priced round.
Open roles found (Power Systems Engineer, Senior Project Engineer) are power-systems/project-engineering roles, not senior/staff software engineering positions.

No match to the person's top-weighted themes (consumer, applied AI verticals, agent tooling, databases/distributed systems, SaaS) — this is grid-measurement hardware/telecom engineering, an industrial energy-infrastructure company.
assessment.rationale: Reactive Technologies is a legitimate, technically substantial operating company with real utility customers and credible investors (Breakthrough Energy Ventures, M&G, BGF), but it sits entirely outside this person's stated interest areas (no AI, consumer, SaaS, fintech, or infra/database angle), is UK-headquartered, and is a mature ~16-year-old company with a mid-size team hiring for power-systems roles rather than software engineering — so it scores low despite being a real business.
assessment.summary: Reactive Technologies is a London-based grid-technology company (founded 2010) that measures power grid inertia and stability in real time via its Grid-Sonar/GridVerix platform, serving utilities and grid operators. It just secured €19M in EIB financing to expand across Europe, adding to over $94M raised to date from investors including Breakthrough Energy Ventures and M&G.
assessment.product: Grid-Sonar hardware and the GridVerix software platform provide real-time measurement of grid inertia, system strength, and oscillations for electric utilities and system operators.
assessment.team: Co-founded in 2010 by CEO Marc Borrett and Dr. Heikki Huomo (former Nokia technology development lead); ~50-79 employees per LinkedIn/PitchBook/LeadIQ, with HQ in London, commercial offices on both US coasts, in the UAE and Australia, and an R&D center in Finland.
assessment.funding: Total funding reported at $94.6M over 11 rounds; a £25M (~$31.4M) Series D closed May 2024 led by M&G's Catalyst fund with BGF and Breakthrough Energy Ventures; most recently €19M in EIB debt financing announced September 2026 to fund European expansion.
redFlags: Most recent funding is EIB debt financing, not an equity round, which is a weaker growth/conviction signal.
No senior/staff software engineering roles found on the careers page — hiring is concentrated in power-systems and commercial functions.
greenFlags: Technically deep founding team with real domain expertise (comms engineering, ex-Nokia)
Real, deployed product used by utilities/grid operators rather than a concept-stage offering
Backed by credible specialist investors including Breakthrough Energy Ventures and M&G

name: Reply Next
evidence: Headline: AI platform Reply Next secures €400K pre-seed funding

Summary: Reply Next, an AIplatform for managing the digital presence of businesses with multiplelocations, has raised €400,000 in pre-seed funding. The round was led byindependent investment firm 4Founders Cap...

assessment.whatTheyDo: Spanish AI platform that lets brands with many physical locations manage reviews, messages, ratings and search presence (Google Maps, App Store, Google Play, Booking, etc.) from one dashboard, with AI agents that auto-respond to customers.
matchedInterests: Applied AI in a specific vertical (legal, health, finance, logistics)
concerns: Headquartered in Madrid, Spain, outside the US, so joining as a US-based employee means visa, relocation or a time-zone gap; scored lower for this reason
Review/reputation management is a crowded category, and the AI auto-reply layer looks thin and may be close to a GPT wrapper; no evidence found of proprietary technology or data
Very small €400K pre-seed suggests a tiny team with limited runway and few engineering hires soon
The product site returned no readable content, and no careers page or open roles were found, so there is no signal about senior or staff engineering hiring
Funding is earmarked for technology and sales team expansion, and the stated goal is more AI agents; there is no evidence of deep technical work
assessment.rationale: This is a real, operating product with paying customers (reportedly 50+) and a founder with 9 years at Google, but the category is crowded and the AI layer is not shown to be technically differentiated. Because the company is Spain-based, has a tiny round and lists no engineering roles, it is a weak fit for a US engineer looking for a high-leverage technical role. Confidence is medium because there is little independent information about the tech and team.
assessment.summary: Reply Next is a Madrid-based startup founded in 2023 by Miguel Peñate, a former Google apps lead. It sells a multi-location reputation and digital-presence management platform with AI agents that reply to reviews and messages. It raised a €400K pre-seed led by 4Founders Capital, with angels Juanjo Mostazo and David Alcobero. It appears to be a real but small SaaS business in a crowded niche, and it is offshore for a US-based candidate.
assessment.product: A single dashboard for brands with hundreds or thousands of physical locations to monitor and respond to reviews, ratings, messages and search results across Google Maps, Google Play, App Store, Booking, Instagram and Facebook. AI agents reply to customers according to brand guidelines, flag issues and opportunities, and monitor competitors. The company reportedly targets restaurant and hospitality chains.
assessment.team: Founder and CEO Miguel Peñate is a telecommunications/ICT engineer (Universitat Ramon Llull, 2009-2013) who reportedly spent about 9 years at Google, where he was head of Apps. Team size and other team members were not found.
assessment.funding: €400K pre-seed announced 2026-09-24, led by 4Founders Capital (an independent investment firm), with business angels Juanjo Mostazo and David Alcobero. Funds are earmarked for technology and sales team expansion, product development and new AI agents.
redFlags: Non-US headquarters (Madrid)
Crowded review-management category, and the AI layer may be a thin wrapper
No careers page or open roles found
The product site returned no readable content
Team size and technical depth are unverified
greenFlags: Real shipped product, reportedly 50+ customers
Founder has 9 years at Google, in a product-facing apps role
A modest round, not an oversized seed with no product
The company is small enough that early engineers would likely be close to product decisions
